# Recovery Requirements Checklist: Quota-Aware Harness Resume

**Purpose**: Review the completeness, clarity, consistency, and measurability of the high-risk lifecycle, persistence, native-context, pool-suppression, observability, and secret-safety requirements before implementation approval
**Created**: 2026-09-30
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact for peer review at the implementation-approval and PR-review boundary. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are quota exhaustion, quota waiting, renewal eligibility, resume reservation, resumed execution, repeated exhaustion, and operator blocking all defined as distinct lifecycle stages? [Completeness, Spec §User Stories 1–3, Spec §FR-001–FR-011]
- [ ] CHK002 Are startup, dynamic reload, restart, dispatch, retry, reconciliation, cancellation, terminal cleanup, and partial-failure requirements documented wherever they apply to quota-paused work? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006, Spec §FR-009, Spec §FR-012, Spec §SC-005]
- [ ] CHK003 Are durable-state requirements complete for every field needed to recover a wait without retaining prompts, outputs, credentials, or raw provider responses? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005, Spec §SC-007]
- [ ] CHK004 Are persistence-failure and malformed-state outcomes explicitly defined, including whether execution remains active, waiting, or operator blocked? [Completeness, Spec §Edge Cases, Plan §Technical Context]
- [ ] CHK005 Are requirements for removing or retaining quota-wait state defined for cancellation, loss of eligibility or required labels, terminal transitions, and workspace cleanup? [Completeness, Spec §FR-012]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK006 Is a “recognized quota exhaustion” distinguishable from transport, authentication, permission, billing, free-text, and ordinary worker failures using objective criteria? [Clarity, Spec §FR-001, Spec §FR-017]
- [ ] CHK007 Is “stable quota-pool scope” defined precisely enough to determine which new and resumed tasks are suppressed and which unrelated tasks remain eligible? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK008 Is “trustworthy renewal time” defined with validation and stale/malformed timestamp handling rather than left to provider interpretation? [Clarity, Spec §FR-007–FR-008]
- [ ] CHK009 Is the bounded unknown-renewal recheck policy specified with an operator-visible configurable interval and a prohibition on tight loops? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008, Spec §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK010 Is native conversation identity defined separately from the durable workflow checkpoint and workspace so that each preservation guarantee is unambiguous? [Clarity, Spec §FR-010, Spec §FR-016]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK011 Are slot release and pool-wide suppression requirements consistent with normal global/per-state concurrency and routing rules? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004, Spec §FR-007, Spec §FR-012]
- [ ] CHK012 Are persist-before-release and persist-before-resume obligations consistent across the feature specification, state model, and harness contract? [Consistency, Spec §FR-005–FR-006, Plan §Phase 1]
- [ ] CHK013 Are the native-resume and no-fresh-thread requirements consistent across normal renewal, restart recovery, missing continuation, mismatched workspace, and failed resume scenarios? [Consistency, Spec §FR-009–FR-011, Spec §FR-016]
- [ ] CHK014 Is Codex-only delivery consistently bounded while the harness-neutral contract specifies future-adapter obligations without implying Claude or GitHub Copilot implementation? [Consistency, Spec §FR-015, Spec §Out of Scope]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK015 Can pre-renewal suppression be objectively measured across repeated polls and service restart for every task sharing the exhausted pool? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002]
- [ ] CHK016 Does the dispatchability target define a measurable start point, deadline, and concurrency exception for renewed eligible work? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-003]
- [ ] CHK017 Can idempotence be objectively established as at most one active attempt and zero duplicate resume dispatches across duplicate signals, polls, restart, and simultaneous eligibility changes? [Measurability, Spec §FR-009, Spec §SC-004]
- [ ] CHK018 Are observability outcomes measurable for all waiting tasks, including differentiation from retrying and operator-blocked work and disclosure of native-continuation availability? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-006]

## Scenario and Edge-Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK019 Are requirements defined for a second quota exhaustion during a resumed turn, including replacement of timing data and prevention of duplicate work? [Coverage, Spec §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK020 Are requirements defined for duplicate quota signals, simultaneous renewal eligibility, stale monitor messages, and repeated reconciliation polls? [Coverage, Spec §FR-009, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK021 Are requirements defined for unavailable, rejected, missing, or issue/workspace-mismatched native continuation references without any fresh-thread fallback? [Coverage, Spec §FR-016, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK022 Are recovery requirements defined when persisted records are missing, corrupt, from an unknown version, or cannot be written atomically? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases, Spec §FR-005–FR-006]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK023 Are log and status requirements specific about stable outcome categories and applicable issue, session, harness, pool, renewal, and recovery context? [Completeness, Spec §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK024 Are secret-exclusion requirements comprehensive across persisted state, logs, status responses, prompts, issue comments, and raw provider payloads? [Security, Spec §FR-013, Spec §SC-007]
- [ ] CHK025 Are the performance and capacity expectations for recovery latency, pool-index reconstruction, and slot release quantified for the stated operating scale? [Measurability, Spec §SC-003, Plan §Technical Context]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK026 Is the assumption that Codex exposes a resumable native conversation identity documented together with the required operator-block outcome when that dependency fails? [Assumption, Spec §FR-010, Spec §FR-016]
- [ ] CHK027 Are dynamic configuration reload semantics clear about which future decisions change and which historical quota signals or durable records remain unchanged? [Clarity, Spec §FR-014]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `$speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `$speckit-specify` and `$speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
